question.text: Within how many working days must a liquid fund pay redemption proceeds?

explanation.text: The Logic: Liquid funds are designed to provide near-cash liquidity, and the regulatory turnaround-time for paying out redemption proceeds is 1 working day from the redemption date. This is faster than the 3 working day window applicable to equity and other open-ended schemes, because liquid funds hold short-tenor, highly liquid instruments that can be sold and settled quickly. The Trap: "3 working days" is the payout window for equity and most other open-ended schemes, not liquid funds. "Same day" describes the optional Instant Access Facility offered up to a cap (Rs. 50,000 or 90% of the folio value, whichever is lower) on top of the regular T+1 payout — it is not the regular redemption deadline. "5 working days" is too long for any mutual fund redemption. Note: The cited NISM Series V-B workbook pages (152-153, 184) describe the same-day Instant Access Facility with a Rs. 50,000 or 90 percent limit but do not explicitly state the 1 working day regular payout deadline for liquid funds. The framing above reflects general SEBI regulatory practice.
